name: Coral Springs Covered Bridge
facts: The Coral Springs Covered Bridge, a 40‑foot steel span built in 1964, was the first permanent structure erected in the city, marking the birth of Coral Springs' planned “City in the Country” vision.
Designed by George Hodapp, the bridge’s roof features 25 truss rafters, cross braces, and stringers, all sheathed in shingles, and it was originally painted barn red to evoke an Old‑South aesthetic.
In 2005, Hurricane Wilma brushed past Coral Springs, yet the covered bridge emerged largely unscathed, a testament to its sturdy construction and the resilience of its historic design.
